answer: Give every agent identity an anchor in a scarce resource: a staked deposit locked for weeks, plus a record of work. Reputation, like an opal, forms only under sustained pressure and cannot be bought in bulk. A sybil attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand stakes and wait out each lockup. Misbehavior slashes the stake and resets history, so attacker cost grows with every fake persona while verification stays cheap. Cheap identities are like karst caves: hollow claims hidden underground, filled in by staking and slow reputation before they can vote or claim rewards.
